chapter: New York dance halls and one-nighters
title: Objections to the dance and La Rocca's crowd-rousing tricks
summary: People said the music was sexual and ruined girls' morals. La Rocca describes sneaking off the stand while the crowd kept rhythm and imitating a woman's holler from his horn to whip the room up.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now what did people object to in the dance?

Well they said we had a sexual music that we were ruining the morals of the girls. They, people would get out there and they'd forget they were dancing, standing in one spot and starting moving around. In other words the great masters tried to move them. But they didn't succeed. I guess ours was like wine or good wine. When the people would get interested in our music. They'd stand there. Some of them would dance around. Stand there and they just moved themselves like worms. And many of the times we'd sneak off to a bandstand. We'd play low. Very low. Very low. And one by one we'd sneak off the bandstand. There was nobody on the stand. These people with their feet were keeping the rhythm. Perfect rhythm on, on you know with the scraping of their feet on the floor. All of a sudden someone would look at the bandstand. There'd be nobody there and you'd talk about a howl. Well to begin. Let me tell you about a certain psychology I used to use. Of course I'm stupid. But I know it takes one monkey to start clapping and hollering and the rest will follow. In my home I had a way that I could imitate a woman's voice. Holler. Whoooo. Just like that. And nobody knew where it would come. It would come out the horn and look like it was a hundred feet away. Before they'd know where it was coming from. Mr. Schultz many times would put people out and they didn't do a thing. It was that hollering. I'd get them so they would be in ecstasy. They wouldn't know where they'd be hollering and stomping more and more and more. And they'd be dropping ten, twenty, and fifty dollar bills in the sugar can. And the more I'd hollered they wouldn't leave the floor. They'd have to take us off the bandstand and get us away so the people could go buy refreshments. That was both at Rice Webbers and this place. 1922 we were relegated to a dance hall. We went to work at Healy's. It was turning into a dance hall for 60 of us only. I worked there about five weeks. Wait, I had my story. Before we went to the dance place, I went on a series of one night stands. stuff
